hooks.text: A secret military blunder caused France's deadliest train disaster.
Why did France hide its deadliest train crash for ninety years?
France's deadliest train disaster was not an unavoidable accident.

title: Why Was France’s Deadliest Train Crash Kept Secret? ⚠️
description: The 1917 Saint-Michel-de-Maurienne derailment remains the deadliest rail disaster in French history. Discover how a series of ignored warnings and military blunders was kept hidden for 90 years.

beats.text: A secret military blunder caused France's deadliest train disaster.
beats.visual: photograph of the wreckage of the Saint-Michel-de-Maurienne train derailment, 1917

beats.text: In 1917, over 1,000 French soldiers boarded a mountain train.
beats.visual: photograph of French World War I soldiers returning from the front, 1917

beats.text: Many believe a simple mechanical failure caused the tragic derailment.
beats.visual: historical postcard of the steep railway tracks in the Maurienne Valley, 1910

beats.text: But a transport officer forced one engine to pull nineteen coaches.
beats.visual: photograph of a 4-6-0 steam locomotive of the PLM railway, 1915
subjects: Chemins de fer de Paris à Lyon et à la Méditerranée

beats.text: Most officers actually abandoned the train for a faster express.
beats.visual: photograph of railway officers at Modane station, 1917

beats.text: The overloaded coaches lost their brakes, killing hundreds of soldiers.
beats.visual: photograph of the burned railway carriage wreckage near Saint-Michel-de-Maurienne, 1917

beats.text: The army then hid this tragic failure for ninety years.
